goal: Independent Windows Snipping Tool replacement retaining Win+Shift+S
reference: Microsoft.ScreenSketch 11.2608.41.0 installed on the local PC
decisions: Keep PNG persistence independent of clipboard publication.
Use local Windows OCR, ZXing for QR, DXGI FP16 for HDR correction, and a child FFmpeg process with WASAPI tracks for recording.
Use the documented OS Click to Do entry point on supported PCs and a local OCR action panel otherwise.
Offer content framing through a local perimeter heuristic and Bing visual search through the browser.
Fetch verified, pinned upstream archives during dependency restore. Publish source and build scripts.
Review a rectangle, window, or full-screen selection before commitment by default. Keep per-capture PNG saving independent of clipboard copy.
verified: Dependencies restore from pinned archives and the release builds with warnings treated as errors under Windows PowerShell.
The packaged WinForms editor opens and displays a synthetic PNG.
The editor Text Actions menu opens and displays OCR word boxes and redaction commands.
Freeform transparency survives opening and exporting quick markup.
Local OCR recognizes synthetic text and content framing bounds the synthetic foreground.
Two actual silent screen segments record, pause, resume, concatenate, and decode as MP4.
MP4 trim and GIF export decode successfully.
The prior packaged executable starts and exits cleanly after extraction.
The physical shortcut smoke opens the Win+Shift+S overlay on the tested desktop.
Off-focus Escape routing reaches an isolated message target and stops after the overlay is detached.
The native Windows share manager can be obtained for a desktop window.
The review stage supports move and resize within the desktop, and final capture uses the adjusted source pixels.
The no-save choice skips PNG and directory creation. The enabled control case writes a PNG.
pendingVerification: Physical shortcut to completed paste and an integrated rerun of off-focus keyboard routing on an idle desktop.
Live microphone and system audio synchronization, HDR monitor color, and sending through a Windows share target.
Visual and behavioral parity with all native app screens and OS-integrated features.
